pairs.difference: A: the sneakers scatter cobalt, mint, lime, magenta and orange across laces, collar and sole trim, all at full strength on an orange and pale yellow set. That gives 5.49 hue families, above the real maximum of 4.78, with no quiet local color on the shoe. B: the candle stays cream, brass and wood against one cyan field, about 4.2 families, and only the flame is a strong accent.
pairs.fix: Make the sneaker two colors only: blue upper and plain white sole. Use white laces and remove the green, pink and orange trim.

pairs.difference: B: the mirror's wall is a dull grey-mauve at 0.095 background chroma, well below the real minimum of 0.138, and the stone floor drifts to warm cream under an orange-gold frame. A: the drink sits on a loud clean violet, slightly above the real range at 0.24, with orange, cyan and pink kept in small separate shapes as on the real cards. Weak call, because A is also loud.
pairs.fix: Paint the wall a clean bright violet with a simple diamond pattern, make the stone floor cool light grey, and use a yellower, less orange gold on the frame.

pairs.difference: B: the feeder has a pure orange roof and pure yellow boards with orange-brown shadows. The trunk is the same orange family, so the lens merges feeder and tree, and the pale park behind sits at 0.08 background chroma, below the real 0.117. Shadow chroma of 0.61 is also below range. A: the navy calculator on clean yellow, with cyan keys as the one accent, is a blue-against-gold split like the real camera card.
pairs.fix: Make the wood a natural light pine with soft grey-brown shadows, the roof a muted brick red, and the trunk a cool grey-brown. Make the park behind a clean bright green and blue.

pairs.difference: A: the moon is cream and tan with an orange-brown shadow side and orange rim. The whole sphere is warm-tinted, with subject chroma of 0.06 and 1.72 hue families, both below the real range. Lessons show this neutral-turned-cream habit on generated cards. B: the brass bugle with a red cord on cyan has one clear hero hue and one accent. Its warm mass does merge into one orange in the lens, so the call is weak.
pairs.fix: Make the moon a cool pale grey, with soft blue-grey shadows in the craters and on the dark side, and no orange at the edge.

pairs.difference: B: the pool bar carries cyan water, green stools, purple grapes, magenta and orange drinks, yellow pineapple and brown thatch, at 7.05 hue families, above the real maximum of 6.45. Each object is at pure fruit-stand color and nothing leads. A: the cabin holds to red-orange roof, brown logs and green and blue surroundings, with grey stone as rest. It has the same hero-against-setting order as the real scene cards.
pairs.fix: Keep the bar to three color groups: turquoise water, warm wood and pale stone. Use muted olive stools and only one bright drink as the accent.

pairs.difference: A: this is the same pool bar, with 7.05 hue families above the real range and pure green, purple, orange and cyan objects competing. B: the gate stays a tight violet and grey scheme, with iron and stone near neutral at subject chroma 0.043. Small yellow lantern glows are the single accent, and the shadows stay lavender, related to the sky.
pairs.fix: Keep the bar to three color groups: turquoise water, warm wood and pale stone. Use muted olive stools and only one bright drink as the accent.

pairs.difference: A: the locker is orange on every face. Its shelves, inside and vents go orange to red-orange, and even the wood floor and book pages pull the same way, so only the purple wall relieves it. B: the armchair keeps a rich crimson with darker red shadows and natural brown legs on a calm mint wall, a clean complementary split. Numbers do not separate them, so this is a low-confidence read of the orange shadows.
pairs.fix: Paint the locker a slightly duller painted-metal orange, make the inside shadows cool brown-purple, and make the floor pale neutral wood.

pairs.difference: A: the bronze lamp on a yellow-green burst has a pale glass neutral and a warm metal hero. B: the green map on pink has cream borders and small red and cyan accents. Both stay inside the real range on every field and both have clear hero and background hue roles. Color gives no reason to choose.

B: the neck pillow is one pure electric blue from highlight to shadow, against an equally loud pink, so hero and background both shout with nothing neutral between them. A: the lantern has gunmetal near-neutral on lime with a small flame accent, giving a resting mass, though its warm share, hue count and shadow chroma all fall below the real range. The call follows the lesson direction that generated cards run louder, not the numbers alone.
pairs.fix: Make the pillow a softer denim blue with lighter, slightly grey fabric highlights and deeper navy folds, and make the pink background paler and calmer.

pairs.difference: B: the fruit plate has every piece at pure hue, red melon, orange, strawberries and green grapes, at subject chroma 0.17 above the real 0.164. The pale wood behind falls to 0.094, below range, and warm share of 0.853 sits at the real limit, so the card leans orange. A: the candy corn has three simple bands against a clean purple wall, and the shadow on the table goes plum, like the plum shadow under the real glove.
pairs.fix: Lower the fruit to natural colors with soft pink-red melon, muted oranges and duller green grapes. Set it on a clean, more colorful background, and give the shadows a cool plum tint.

pairs.difference: B: the card is almost entirely warm at warm share 0.999, above the real 0.853. It combines an orange horse, orange floor, hot pink wall and red saddle, and the black mane turns brown in the lens, so there is no cool mass or neutral anywhere. A: the green binoculars with blue lenses and neutral black rims give cool relief against the yellow wood, at warm share 0.787. Both have low shadow chroma.
pairs.fix: Make the wood a pale natural beech, keep the mane a true cool black, and put cool blue-violet in the floor shadows. Use a cooler pink or a light blue wall.

pairs.difference: B: the fan is a pure neon violet at subject chroma 0.226, above the real 0.189, against a loud yellow, so hero and background compete at full strength with no neutral but the small wood sticks. A: the spider is dark slate near-neutral on orange with small red spots, so the hero rests the eye. It sits low at 0.041 subject chroma, but its role split is clean.
pairs.fix: Make the fan a softer plum-purple paper with darker muted folds, and calm the yellow background to a lighter, plainer gold.

pattern: Generated cards still show themselves in three ways. Every object sits at pure hue, so hero and background are equally loud with no neutral mass, and many separate hue families compete. Warm bias runs through the card: true neutrals turn cream or tan, wood goes orange, and shadows stay orange-brown where real cards drop to cool plum, blue or grey. The result is a card pulled warm with no cool relief. The strongest signals here are excess hue count (pool bar) and warm share near 1.0 (rocking horse). Several calls are only moderate confidence, because some suspect cards are muted, not loud, and p08 gave no color reason to choose.
